section: I. Derived operations and the projection formula
title: Exchange identities as a duality programme
body: The phrase “$D$ ‘échange’” places the immersion calculation within a programme relating direct image, exceptional direct image, pullback and exceptional inverse image through duality. The displayed closed-immersion argument actually gives a calculation using acyclicity and injectivity, so it should not be catalogued as an entirely unsupported assertion merely because the prose calls it “essentiellement trivial.” These pages add a concrete organizational principle to the README's SGA 4/5 mapping request, but the supplied context has no earlier scan against which its first occurrence can be dated.

section: I. Derived operations and the projection formula
title: Flat resolutions and the quotient by quasi-isomorphisms
body: “Tout Module $F$ … est quotient d'un plat” is used to construct bounded-above flat resolutions, and the insertion “ça passe au quotient par quasi-isomorphisme” supplies the key descent assertion for derived tensor. A full proof must control acyclic flat complexes under tensoring and the comparison of resolutions; the manuscript gives the generators $A_U$ but does not write out those verifications here. The modern construction by K-flat resolutions supplies the corresponding framework (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., §21.17–18, [Tag 06YV](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06YV)); this comparison restates the mathematical mechanism without importing modern notation into the transcription.

section: I. Derived operations and the projection formula
title: The explicit question about general topoi
kind: self-flagged: a step he himself marks as unverified
body: The marginal question “est-ce vrai dans le contexte des topos généraux ?” is attached to the paragraph asserting preservation of flat modules and the resulting tensor comparison, so its scope should remain local to that argument. For morphisms of ringed topoi, the modern derived-pullback construction preserves suitable K-flat resolutions and commutes with derived tensor (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., [Tag 06YV](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06YV), Lemmas 21.18.1–4). This confirms a precise modern formulation of the question rather than establishing which axioms the undated draft intended by “topos généraux.”

section: I. Derived operations and the projection formula
title: Nonflat base change is a later extension
body: “Remarque sur changement de base non plat” replaces the earlier flatness restriction by a derived pullback defined through flat resolutions, followed on 106 by transitivity “sans hypothèse sur $f,g$ composables.” Relative to 102, this adds a broader construction; it does not retract the flat special case or license replacing every visible $f^*$ by $\mathbb Lf^*$. The modern comparison is the monoidal and compositional structure in The Stacks Project Authors (n.d., [Tag 06YV](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06YV), Lemmas 21.18.3–4).

section: I. Derived operations and the projection formula
title: Bounds behind global hyper-Tor
body: The marginal “Mais il faut supposer … que $\Gamma_X$ est de dim … finie !” qualifies the unrestricted global hyper-Tor construction, while another note treats a bounded-below second argument for derived internal Hom. These qualifications add evidence that the author is tracking the distinction between existence in a selected derived-category range and preservation of bounds, rather than simply manipulating formal symbols. The small wording of the first qualification is uncertain, so it should not be used as a fully precise general nonexistence theorem for unbounded derived functors.

section: I. Derived operations and the projection formula
title: The injective proof is corrected on the same sheet
body: The proposed proof of adjunction is qualified by the marginal “Attention, [ne marche que si] $f$ est plat,” followed by a reduction to a generator and a localization diagram. What is withdrawn is the unrestricted use of that injective-resolution argument, not the adjunction statement itself; the replacement argument is sketched rather than fully checked, and its generator decoration is a low-confidence reading. Both the initial argument and its same-page correction therefore belong to the record, with the uncertainty of the marginal wording retained.

section: I. Derived operations and the projection formula
title: Internal-Hom compatibility and its local verification
body: The “Formule de projection” on this sheet is the derived internal-Hom comparison, supported by the external-Hom adjunction and the assertion that the localization square permits the needed base change. Its proof obligation is compatibility of those constructions with restriction to the indicated localizations, not an arbitrary base-change theorem for every square. This adds a local-to-global proof strategy to the supplied plan; no corresponding assertion or scan is present in the context register.

section: I. Derived operations and the projection formula
title: Finite coefficient rings force attention to unbounded resolutions
body: The warning that $\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z$ is not a field and need not have finite global Tor dimension explains the move from degree-zero sheaves into $D^-$, while 112 emphasizes that tensor and derived Hom can have unbounded cohomological effects even at a geometric point. The opening remark on 108 explicitly leaves finite-Tor and finite-Ext refinements outside the current scope. This is a methodological precursor to the perfect-complex trace construction on 130–146, not evidence that all finite coefficient modules are perfect. The literal warning about $\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z$ also needs arithmetic scope: squarefree $n$ gives a product of fields, whereas $n=\ell^2$ gives the actual obstruction checked in N10.

section: I. Derived operations and the projection formula
title: The noetherian expectation for relative direct image
kind: self-flagged: a step he himself marks as unverified
body: “C'est peut-être vrai dès que $Y$ est noethérien” concerns finite **relative** cohomological dimension of $f_*$, in the surrounding finite-type discussion, rather than finite absolute cohomological dimension of $Y$. The finite-type-over-a-field case has a direct modern counterpart (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., [Tag 0F10](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F10)), and Illusie (2014, Exposé XVIII_A, Corollary 1.4) proves the relative $\ell$-torsion statement for finite-dimensional noetherian $Y$ with $\ell$ invertible on $Y$. Those results confirm qualified versions; these notes leave the draft's full “merely noetherian” scope unresolved and do not offer the absolute cohomology of a field as a counterexample to it.

section: I. Derived operations and the projection formula
title: A point already exhibits infinite Tor
body: A concrete check of “même si $X$ … un pt géométrique” is $A=\mathbb Z/\ell^2\mathbb Z$ and $M=A/\ell A$: the resolution with every differential multiplication by $\ell$ is exact, while tensoring it with $M$ makes every differential zero. Hence $\operatorname{Tor}_i^A(M,M)\cong M$ for every $i\geq0$, so locally constant finite modules do not automatically give bounded derived tensor products. This is our elementary example, adding an explicit witness to the manuscript's warning, not a claim that the example is written there.
confidence: high — exactness and the tensor calculation are checked directly.

section: I. Derived operations and the projection formula
title: Compact-support projection and the literal formulas
body: The main theorem says “un isom. canonique bifonctoriel,” but its printed LaTeX reading follows the manuscript's shorthand without inserting a missing pullback, and the smaller inserted proposition repeats the same displayed expression on both sides. The expected typed comparison is $Rf_!L\otimes^{\mathbf L}M\to Rf_!(L\otimes^{\mathbf L}f^*M)$, as in Deligne (1973, XVII, Proposition 5.2.9), but that expectation is a research-note interpretation, not a corrected transcription. The scope of the small proposition must also retain its explicit “sous réserve $f_*$ de dim. ch. finie.”

section: I. Derived operations and the projection formula
title: Functoriality is expressly left to verify
kind: self-flagged: a step he himself marks as unverified
body: “Il faut vérifier que c'est un hom fonctoriel pour les catégories dérivées” explicitly leaves a verification after constructing the comparison on resolutions. The subsequent reductions to degree-zero terms and an étale generator, and the marginal proposal to use proper base change on geometric fibres, address why the comparison should be an isomorphism but do not themselves supply every naturality and resolution-independence diagram. This adds a precise unfinished compatibility problem to the README's S19 comparison programme.

section: II. Künneth, nonproper supports and the Lefschetz programme
title: Künneth is reduced to two projection steps
body: “S'obtient en appliquant 2 fois la formule de projection” compresses the compact-support Künneth proof, and the margin records that projection is recovered by specializing one structural morphism to an isomorphism. The page also rewrites its flatness assumptions, so the flat-sheaf special case should be distinguished from the derived statement and from a formula without Tor contributions. Deligne (1973, XVII, Theorem 5.4.3) is a published comparison locator for the compact-support result; identity of the canonical comparison maps remains part of the draft-to-print study.

section: II. Künneth, nonproper supports and the Lefschetz programme
title: One proper factor and the characteristic restriction
body: The argument beginning “si $X$ ou $Y$ propre sur $k$” combines proper base change with projection and is explicitly distinguished on 120 from statements requiring $n$ prime to the characteristic. The Stacks Project Authors (n.d., [Tag 0F14](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F14), Lemma 59.97.2(2)) confirms this one-proper-factor formula for finite-type schemes over a separably closed field and arbitrary $\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z$ complexes, without assuming $n$ invertible. This comparison supports the manuscript's distinction rather than transferring the later prime-to-characteristic condition backwards to all Künneth formulas in the package.

section: II. Künneth, nonproper supports and the Lefschetz programme
title: The nonproper prime-to-characteristic expectation
body: “Je pense qu'on doit encore avoir la formule … si $n$ est premier à la caractéristique” asserts the nonproper ordinary-cohomology expectation and proposes local duality as a route. A modern precise statement is The Stacks Project Authors (n.d., [Tag 0F1P](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F1P), Lemma 59.97.9): both schemes may be nonproper, provided they are finite type over a separably closed field and $n$ is invertible. This confirms the assertion in that scope, while neither the manuscript nor that modern comparison establishes priority for the proposed proof method.

section: II. Künneth, nonproper supports and the Lefschetz programme
title: An explicit characteristic-p failure in degree one
body: For algebraically closed $k$ of characteristic $p$, Artin–Schreier gives $H^1_{\mathrm{ét}}(\mathbb A_k^2,\mathbb F_p)=k[x,y]/\{h^p-h\}$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., [Tag 0A3J](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A3J)). The class of $xy$ does not come from the sum of the two one-variable cohomology groups: an equality $xy=a(x)+b(y)+h^p-h$ would leave, after discarding pure-variable monomials, a mixed polynomial $q$ with $q^p-q=xy$, which is impossible by its highest total degree. This checks the manuscript's failure claim and is consistent with the doubtful addition “même pour $H^1$,” but it gives no permission to remove that paleographic doubt from the frozen text.
confidence: high — the Artin–Schreier quotient and the mixed-monomial obstruction are explicit.

section: II. Künneth, nonproper supports and the Lefschetz programme
title: The Verdier priority remark remains conditional
body: “[La formule] aurait d'abord été établie par Verdier … en utilisant le th. de dualité globale” is a hedged historical attribution, not an unqualified bibliographic statement. The package adds evidence of the author's reported understanding of that history, but neither supplied context file contains a contemporaneous source settling it. The later exposition and its publication history are comparison material, not a basis for upgrading “aurait” to a verified priority claim.

section: II. Künneth, nonproper supports and the Lefschetz programme
title: The support obstruction to ordinary direct-image projection
body: The manuscript says the ordinary-direct-image analogue would force a vanishing off an open set “ce qui n'est pas vrai si $f$ non propre.” An explicit model is $j:\mathbb G_{m,k}\hookrightarrow\mathbb A^1_k$, with $k$ algebraically closed, $L=\Lambda$ on $\mathbb G_m$ and $M=j_!\Lambda$ for a finite field of coefficients: at a geometric point over $0$, $(Rj_*L)\otimes^{\mathbf L}M$ has zero stalk, whereas $Rj_*(L\otimes j^*M)$ has nonzero $H^0$ stalk. This adds a concrete boundary calculation to the manuscript's mechanism; the connected punctured strict-local neighbourhood gives the nonzero constant section.
confidence: high — the two stalks differ already in degree zero.

section: II. Künneth, nonproper supports and the Lefschetz programme
title: The locally constant variant needs its actual scope
body: “Une démonstration presque immédiate” reduces the locally constant-cohomology variant to $M=A_Y$, but the paragraph stops at “où” and does not display the whole dévissage. A secure overlapping theorem is projection for a perfect target complex over any morphism of ringed topoi (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., [Tag 0944](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0944)); this does not by itself settle the manuscript's broader finite-cohomological-dimension/locally-constant variant over a nonregular finite ring. In particular, the finite module in N10 is locally constant at a point and pseudo-coherent there, yet not perfect, so these hypotheses must not be conflated.

section: II. Künneth, nonproper supports and the Lefschetz programme
title: Curves, singular coefficients and rationality of L-functions
body: “Il semble que pour les courbes, on récupère … (sans résolution des singularités) … $\rightsquigarrow$ rationalité des fonctions $L$” is a proposed application of the formalism, not a proved curve theorem on this page. A proof would have to identify the extension-by-zero or immersion argument, justify the local terms for the singular coefficient sheaf, and then pass from the trace identities to the Euler product/determinant identity. The finished SGA 5 provides distinct comparison destinations for Lefschetz and for rationality, but the present evidence does not identify this draft with a particular circulated version (Grothendieck, 1977, Exposé III; Illusie, 1977, volume contents).

section: II. Künneth, nonproper supports and the Lefschetz programme
title: Formalism is deliberately prioritized over applications
body: The insertion “th. de bidualité (= dualité locale)” and the sentence “je préfère en compléter les lignes essentielles” locate the author's next work within a chosen formal programme rather than an exhausted list of applications. The juxtaposition of Lefschetz–Cartier and rationality is a research lead, but the overlapping cancellations prevent a confident reconstruction of every proposed transition. This adds manuscript evidence for the README's SGA 4/5 placement while differing in subject from the Hodge-index use of “Lefschetz” in **WG H9**.

section: II. Künneth, nonproper supports and the Lefschetz programme
title: Fixed points require local multiplicities
body: The schematic equality with “nb de pts fixes” is immediately qualified by “avec grain de sel,” and isolated fixed points are said to require suitable multiplicities. The later promise “On donnera l'approche de Verdier” leaves both the general coefficient-sheaf construction and the promised elementary derivation to be developed beyond this opening paragraph. This adds a trace/local-term programme, not a count of fixed points with multiplicity one; comparison with the finished exposition belongs at Grothendieck (1977, Exposé III, §§3–4).

section: III. Traces over finite rings and perfect complexes
title: Why reduction to a finite field is rejected
body: “Il ne serait pas admissible de se limiter à des corps” makes the arithmetic objective explicit: the author wants information finer than the fixed-point count modulo $\ell$. The obstruction is that cohomology modules over $\mathbb Z/\ell^\nu\mathbb Z$ need not be free, so the usual degreewise finite-projective trace cannot simply be applied to each of them. The subsequent Bourbaki/$\ell$-adic discussion is a workaround under consideration, whereas 128–136 introduces a finite-level complex-theoretic construction; neither passage is a withdrawal of the demand for integral information.

section: III. Traces over finite rings and perfect complexes
title: The finite-level-to-adic passage is an expectation
body: “On a envie de dire … conséquence formelle, par passage à la limite” proposes deriving the adic formula from finite-level trace identities. To make that claim precise one needs compatible coefficient reduction, an appropriate inverse-limit formalism and control of finiteness; the draft supplies no full inverse-limit argument here. The supplied results register has no entry settling this passage, and the clipped upper addition cannot be used to infer a stronger integrality assertion than the legible text supports.

section: III. Traces over finite rings and perfect complexes
title: A perfect complex with nonprojective cohomology
body: Let $A=\mathbb Z/\ell^2\mathbb Z$ and take the two-term complex $P=[A\xrightarrow{\ell}A]$ in degrees $0,1$. It is perfect, with $H^0(P)\cong H^1(P)\cong A/\ell A$ nonprojective, while the trace of its identity is unambiguously $1-1=0$ in $A$ by the finite-projective supertrace formula (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., [Tag 03TI](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03TI)). This gives a concrete reason for the manuscript's replacement of the system of cohomology groups by its complex, and differs from N10 because the **object** here is perfect even though its cohomology modules are not.
confidence: high — all modules, differential, cohomology and traces are explicit.

section: III. Traces over finite rings and perfect complexes
title: The unnamed perfectness criterion
body: The page identifies the intersection of pseudo-coherence and finite Tor dimension with complexes “projectifs de type fini” in finitely many degrees, without introducing the later label “perfect” into its text. Over a ring this is precisely the modern criterion, including control of the representative by a prescribed Tor-amplitude (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., [Tag 0656](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0656), Lemma 15.76.2). The assertion is supplied here as a tool rather than proved in detail, so the draft-to-print comparison should follow the truncation step where the last finitely presented flat module becomes projective.

section: III. Traces over finite rings and perfect complexes
title: Existence of trace is reduced and then addressed
body: On 132, “L'existence … se ramène à prouver” invariance under isomorphism is an unfinished reduction at the page boundary; 134 continues it by vanishing on acyclic bounded finite-projective complexes and short exact sequences. It is therefore a proof sketch completed in these pages, not an indefinitely abandoned existence claim. The corresponding independence-of-representative statement is verified in The Stacks Project Authors (n.d., [Tag 03TI](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03TI)); the manuscript's contribution to the supplied plan is its explicit passage from an alternating expression to a derived invariant.

section: III. Traces over finite rings and perfect complexes
title: Mapping-cylinder additivity must not be enlarged indiscriminately
body: The words “d'additivité pour un mapping cylindre” should be read with their chain-level compatibility data, not promoted to additivity for every endomorphism of an abstract distinguished triangle. The latter statement is false even for perfect complexes: The Stacks Project Authors (n.d., [Tag 087L](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/087L), Lemma 110.65.1) gives a counterexample. This is a boundary for a possible modern reconstruction, not a contradiction of what the manuscript actually states.
confidence: high — the stronger false statement and a primary counterexample are explicitly identified.

section: III. Traces over finite rings and perfect complexes
title: Duality gives the intrinsic trace
body: The phrase “comme une ‘contraction’ au sens tensoriel” turns the degreewise trace into a pairing involving $L^\vee$, biduality and the derived Hom–tensor identification. The modern perfect-duality statement reproduces this mechanism for ringed sites (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., [Tag 0FPP](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FPP), Lemma 21.48.4), while the manuscript itself uses it to recover cyclicity and the supertrace formula. This adds a categorical explanation of the construction rather than requiring free cohomology modules, and the overwritten arguments on 136 remain a separate reading problem.

section: III. Traces over finite rings and perfect complexes
title: The remaining finiteness requirement for global cohomology
kind: self-flagged: a step he himself marks as unverified
body: “Il faut savoir que $\mathbb R\Gamma_X(A_X)$ est bien … de Tor-dim finie” is sharpened by the insertion calling pseudo-coherence known and leaving Tor dimension to the next development. The compact-support proposition on 140–142 supplies the missing type of estimate for $Rf_!$, and gives the needed global-cohomology case when the structural morphism is proper; it is not automatically a proof for every nonproper $R\Gamma$. This distinction is an addition to the context's broad SGA placement and prevents treating the passage to $Rf_!$ as an unnoticed substitution for ordinary cohomology.

section: IV. Tor bounds and cohomological correspondences
title: Uniform Tor bounds versus pointwise finite bounds
body: The manuscript uses one fixed interval for “tout pt géom,” a quantifier that should be retained in any reconstruction. On a disjoint union of infinitely many points, put a copy of $A$ in cohomological degree $-n$ on the $n$th component: this is locally perfect and bounded above, with finite Tor-amplitude at every stalk, but it has no single global finite amplitude interval. The example distinguishes the manuscript's uniform claim from the local perfectness criterion (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., [Tag 08G8](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08G8)); it does not refute the fixed-interval stalkwise criterion on the page.
confidence: high — the degrees and the failure of a uniform lower bound are explicit.

section: IV. Tor bounds and cohomological correspondences
title: The compact-support amplitude estimate
body: The inserted hypothesis “l'Anneau de base soit de torsion” belongs to the proposition, whose proof is described as “Résulte … de Künneth.” For compactifiable $f$ with geometric fibres of dimension at most $d$, Deligne (1973, XVII, Corollary 5.2.8.1 and Proposition 5.2.9) gives $\mathrm{cd}(Rf_!)\leq2d$ for torsion sheaves and the projection comparison. Our inference sends Tor-amplitude $[a,b]$ in cohomological indexing into $[a,b+2d]$; setting $a=-M,b=-N$ then yields the displayed homological $[N-2d,M]$. This supports the direction of the shift without imposing a prime-to-characteristic hypothesis absent from this compact-support argument.

section: IV. Tor bounds and cohomological correspondences
title: The interval letters and the ordinary tensor stay literal
body: The source alternates $N'$, $M$ and overwritten endpoints, changes the proposition's input from $F_\bullet$ on 140 to $L_\bullet$ on 142, and writes an ordinary tensor on the right of the proof's main formula. The words “notations … de degrés inférieurs” and “notation homologique!” favor a consistent interpretation of the negative shift, but do not decide every overwritten letter or authorize adding a derived decoration to the ordinary tensor. The literature comparison in N32 therefore belongs to the notes, while the different readings and alternatives remain fixed in the LaTeX.

section: IV. Tor bounds and cohomological correspondences
title: Degree-zero correspondences and an omitted H-zero
body: The first display equates $\operatorname{Hom}^0$ with an entire $R\Gamma R\mathcal Hom$ expression, although the surrounding chain is explicitly about “correspondances cohomologiques de degré $0$.” The natural type-correct interpretation would take $H^0$ of the latter complex, but no such $H^0$ has been supplied in the transcription. Grothendieck (1977, Exposé III, §§2–3) is a comparison destination for the derived functoriality and correspondence construction, not evidence that the missing characters were present on this sheet.

section: IV. Tor bounds and cohomological correspondences
title: The global trace pairing needs a finite object
body: The trace pairing on 144 is qualified by “si $S$ discret” and finite Tor dimension, whereas 146 explicitly requires both finite Tor dimension and pseudo-coherence for its local trace construction. Finite Tor dimension alone cannot supply a finite-projective trace: an infinite-rank free module over a field already has Tor dimension zero, with no ordinary finite-matrix trace of its identity. The intended global setting may inherit constructibility or finiteness assumptions from preceding work, but those assumptions need to be recovered rather than inferred from the insertion alone.
confidence: high for the infinite-free-module scope test; the intended inherited finiteness hypotheses remain unresolved.

section: IV. Tor bounds and cohomological correspondences
title: A local pairing is cancelled, then the construction restarts
body: The paragraph beginning “Cet accouplement est induit par un accouplement de nature locale” is cancelled on 144, including the doubtful parenthesis “[pas besoin] que $f$ et $g$ soient propres.” Scan 146 restarts with a trace map and cyclic pairings for pseudo-coherent finite-Tor-dimensional complexes, but the two pages do not finish the entire local-to-global Lefschetz–Verdier theorem. This adds evidence of a change in exposition and should not be recorded as a proved rejection of local pairings or as a completed theorem without properness (compare Grothendieck, 1977, Exposé III, §4).

section: IV. Tor bounds and cohomological correspondences
title: The local trace and the symmetry sign
body: The trace diagram and the final equality with “$\operatorname{sym}$” encode cyclicity through the symmetry of the derived tensor category, so the sign rule is part of the construction and not optional decoration. A proof can use local strictly perfect representatives and then check descent and compatibility of evaluation/coevaluation; the ringed-site duality formulation provides this framework (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., [Tag 0FPP](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FPP)). The displayed supertrace and the two composition expressions are written here, but the page stops before a full verification of their compatibility.

section: IV. Tor bounds and cohomological correspondences
title: The deleted boundedness condition has mathematical consequences
body: In the inserted phrase “loc. libre de t.f., et borné,” the words “et borné” are themselves deleted, so they cannot be treated as a surviving hypothesis on this page. An infinite direct sum of contractible two-term free complexes placed in disjoint, successively negative degrees represents the zero, hence perfect, derived object, yet its identity has no finite degreewise alternating sum on that unbounded representative. Thus the literal representative-based formula needs local bounded representatives or another specified interpretation; this is a conditional scope objection, not a reason to restore the deletion or deny the intrinsic trace of the perfect object.
confidence: high — a zero object with an unbounded finite-free representative separates the two assertions.

section: IV. Tor bounds and cohomological correspondences
title: The second composition pairing has a mismatched factor
body: The second displayed pairing reads $R\mathcal Hom(M_\bullet,L_\bullet)\times R\mathcal Hom(L_\bullet,L_\bullet)\to R\mathcal Hom(M_\bullet,M_\bullet)$, with the second factor visibly involving $L$ twice. For the stated $(v,u)\mapsto uv$ composition one expects a second factor $R\mathcal Hom(L_\bullet,M_\bullet)$, as in the opposite-order companion to the preceding line. This is a type-based reading question raised after freezing, not an emendation, and the supplied context contains no parallel scan to adjudicate it.

section: IV. Tor bounds and cohomological correspondences
title: A controlled finite-level compatibility test
body:
A useful intermediate test for the proposed “passage à la limite” is a compatible system of bounded finite-projective complexes over $A_
u=\mathbb Z/\ell^
u\mathbb Z$, with endomorphisms and compatible derived coefficient reduction. Degreewise matrix trace commutes with reduction, so their supertraces form an element of $\varprojlim A_
u=\mathbb Z_\ell$; the additional task is to prove that the geometric cohomology complexes admit the required compatible perfect models. This gives a concrete sufficient mechanism for the manuscript's expectation while leaving that geometric inverse-limit problem open in these pages.
confidence: medium — compatibility of matrix traces is immediate; compatible geometric perfect models have not been proved here.

section: IV. Tor bounds and cohomological correspondences
title: The stronger trace formalism is a comparison target, not a dating proof
body: The progression from pseudo-coherence and Tor dimension to contraction, then to a sheaf-level trace, is closely aligned with the later organization of perfect-complex theory. SGA 6, Exposé I, §8 is a useful locator for a future facsimile collation, while the independently verified Stacks comparisons used above establish the relevant mathematical statements. This adds a concrete target to **S19** in `README.md`, without claiming that these undated sheets are the text of that exposé or that their relative chronology has been established.

section: V. Reused typescripts: separate sources and qualifications
title: The analytic operator-algebra sheet is a separate source
body: Theorem 4.6.6, the kernel description and the integral symbol map (4.6.7) belong to an English typescript on operators, with printed page 72. No sentence on this sheet connects its operator algebra to the later handwritten finite-ring trace construction, so physical adjacency is insufficient evidence for such a mathematical or authorial connection. The source identity remains unresolved; it adds evidence of heterogeneous paper reuse, not a new Grothendieck conjecture inferred from its subject.

section: V. Reused typescripts: separate sources and qualifications
title: The ramification multiplicity question and its internal answers
body: The typed question “under what circumstances this number is an integer” is followed within the reversed printed-page sequence by finite-homological-dimension criteria, residue-extension arguments, and the decomposition theorem. It should therefore be indexed as a question with partial answers in the same reused source, not attributed automatically to the handwritten author's own open programme. The convention on 111 that a local algebra is a localization of a finite algebra is essential when comparing those assertions; the source's full identity and bibliography are not supplied by the context.

section: V. Reused typescripts: separate sources and qualifications
title: Euler characteristics link the two streams only provisionally
body: The finite-resolution/Tor calculation in the ramification typescript invites comparison with the handwritten alternating trace construction: both replace separate homology groups by a finite homological invariant. A useful next check would ask whether the normalized multiplicity calculation factors through an appropriate $K_0$ class before any trace interpretation is asserted. This is our proposed link across reused paper and handwriting, with no explicit cross-reference by the manuscript and no claim that a multiplicity ratio already equals the trace under discussion.

section: V. Reused typescripts: separate sources and qualifications
title: Relative divisors refer to missing earlier definitions
body: The extension of the formulas of §3.2 to relative divisors is said to hold “de façon évidente,” but its definition depends on the unseen sheaf $\underline R_{X/S}$ from §10.1 and on flatness and local finite presentation of $X/S$. A proof or comparison must first recover that relative meromorphic-function sheaf and the precise meaning of transversality; substituting an arbitrary modern definition of relative Cartier divisor would beg the question. This reused French sheet adds a separate source strand and does not establish a link to **WG H9** merely because both concern divisors or Lefschetz-related geometry.

section: V. Reused typescripts: separate sources and qualifications
title: The tame birational lemma is a cited dependency
body: Lemma 6 says the preservation of tame ramification “Follows from Lemmas 6 and 7 of Part I and [A7, Proposition 1.50 of Section 7].” Those references and the definition of tameness must be recovered before the statement is used beyond the typed normal projective setting, and the visible $K^*$/$K'$ discrepancy remains a reading question. The word “tame” does not connect this lemma to the profinite torsion or centralizer problems in **LM4 D.12** and **LM4 F.7** without a further argument.

section: V. Reused typescripts: separate sources and qualifications
title: Normalization does not need to be finite as a module
body: The assertion that the normalization of a one-dimensional local domain is a semilocal PID is correct under the usual Noetherian convention: normalization is semilocal Dedekind, and its invertible ideals are principal (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., [Tags 09IG](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09IG), [09N2](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09N2), [02M9](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02M9)). Thus absence of module-finite normalization or excellence is not by itself a gap in this lemma. What remains to recover is the reused source's convention for “local domain,” which is not spelled out in the surviving statement; a non-Noetherian reading would be a materially different claim.

section: V. Reused typescripts: separate sources and qualifications
title: The power-series assertion requires a missing scope convention
body: The typed parenthesis “then $R=k[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]$” is not a consequence of equal characteristic and a regular system of parameters alone: $R=\mathbb Q[x,y]_{(x,y)}$ is countable and has coefficient field $\mathbb Q$, whereas $\mathbb Q[[x,y]]$ is uncountable. The primary complete-local theorem explicitly assumes completeness (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., [Tag 0C0S](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C0S)). This is a conditional counterexample to the isolated wording, and the right next step is to recover earlier conventions from the reused source before declaring its full theorem false.
confidence: high for the counterexample; unresolved whether the earlier source imposed completeness throughout.

section: V. Reused typescripts: separate sources and qualifications
title: Equal characteristic alone need not give a coefficient field
body: The separate implication “same characteristic so that $R$ has a coefficient field” also needs qualification: $\mathbb Q[x,y]_{(x^2-2,y)}$ is equicharacteristic regular local of dimension two with residue field $\mathbb Q(\sqrt2)$, but its fraction field $\mathbb Q(x,y)$ contains no square root of $2$. Thus no coefficient field can map isomorphically to that residue field, while the complete-local Cohen theorem provides one in its own hypotheses (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., [Tag 032A](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/032A)). This is our second conditional scope test, distinct from N50, not an assertion that the unseen preceding hypotheses were absent.
confidence: high — the residue field and the obstruction inside the rational function field are explicit.

section: V. Reused typescripts: separate sources and qualifications
title: Quadratic transforms use maximal centres in this definition
body: The definition of an immediate quadratic transform localizes $R[Mx^{-1}]$ at a **maximal** ideal, and Lemma 9 then changes a chart basis while preserving the specified local ring. This matters for any attempted comparison with all points of a blowup, since the generic points of exceptional divisors are not covered by the same dimension assertion without changing the formulation. The package adds a source-specific convention; no comparison with resolution or with a register entry should erase the maximal-centre condition.

section: V. Reused typescripts: separate sources and qualifications
title: A cyclic generator-lifting lemma is not a profinite recognition result
body: The lemma lifting a generator through a surjection of finite cyclic groups is proved across 143 and 141, so its proof should be read in the reused source's printed order. It concerns a finite cyclic group and the arithmetic of exponents, whereas **LM4 D.12** and **LM4 F.7** concern full profinite torsion/centralizer questions. The overlap in finite-group vocabulary supplies no proof, counterexample or change of status for either open register entry.

section: V. Reused typescripts: separate sources and qualifications
title: The literal étale criterion admits a dual-number counterexample
body: In condition (c), finite separability of $\kappa(y)/\kappa(x)$ alone does not imply the subsequent equality $m_y=m_xO_y$: $\operatorname{Spec}(k[\varepsilon]/\varepsilon^2)\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is finite, flat and finitely presented, with residue extension $k/k$, but has $m_y=(\varepsilon)\ne0$. Its nonreduced fibre prevents étaleness, in agreement with the criterion requiring étale fibres (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., [Tag 03PC](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03PC), Proposition 59.26.2). This is a counterexample to the isolated residue-field-only wording as transcribed, not to the stronger condition printed immediately afterward or to an unseen theorem elsewhere.
confidence: high — all three literal conditions and the failure of the maximal-ideal equality are directly checked.

section: V. Reused typescripts: separate sources and qualifications
title: The axiomatic étale-topos source is incomplete here
body: “La démonstration … sera donnée dans un instant,” the references to unseen axioms (A)/(A'), and the blanks after “EGA IV” make this sheet an incomplete portion of a separate exposition. Its Lemma 5 states the étale-and-radiciel characterization of open immersions, but the preceding theorem and its promised proof cannot be reconstructed from the single page. This adds a source-identification and dependency task, not a basis for filling the bibliographical blanks or attributing the source's every sentence to the handwritten author.

section: V. Reused typescripts: separate sources and qualifications
title: Two bibliographical leads remain unverified identities
body: Auslander and Rim's (1963) *Ramification index and multiplicity* is a candidate to collate with the first English algebra typescript, and Abhyankar's (1960) *Tame coverings … Part II* is a candidate for the preparation/quadratic-transform source. The publication metadata can be verified, but an exact match of the surviving section titles, theorem numbering and words was not obtained from accessible full texts. These are retrieval leads only: neither authorship attribution nor the expansion of the source's citation keys has been inserted into the transcription.
confidence: low — subject and bibliographical resemblance have not been confirmed by exact textual collation.

section: VII. Title sheets, numbering and page counts
title: Composition of the supplied package
body: There are 49 supplied scans, comprising 25 handwritten subject pages and 24 reused typescript pages, alternating through the sequence; the inventory records no cover sheet and no wholly cancelled draft sheet. These are counts of the supplied scans, not a manuscript assertion that a treatise has 49 pages. The result adds observed source composition to the README's catalogue-level description and does not infer authorship of the reused typescripts.

body: The visible small foliation runs from 97 on scan 098 to 145 on scan 146, independently of the printed numbers on reused sheets. No title sheet in this package states a total such as “19 pages” or a range such as “Pages 1–67”; in particular, the 19 on scan 125 is a printed page number, not a total. The hand or authority responsible for the small foliation is not established here.
